newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CHELSEA, CHESTERFIELD INTO F.A. CUP SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHELSEA, CHESTERFIELD INTO F.A. CUP SEMIFINALS.

text.p: F.A.Cup favourites Chelsea marched confidently into the semifinals with a controlled and comfortable 4-1 win over first division Portsmouth at Fratton Park on Sunday.
Welsh international Mark Hughes put Ruud Gullit's premier league side on the right path when he put them ahead with a superb strike from the edge of the area after 25 minutes.
Two minutes before halftime, Steve Clarke's close range shot was parried by Portsmouth goalkeeper Alan Knight but Dennis Wise was on hand to tap it over the line.
After the break, Roberto Di Matteo went close before combining with Hughes in the 53rd minute to give Italian striker Gianfranco Zola the chance to put the result beyond doubt.

Portsmouth kept battling throughout and were rewarded for their efforts with an 82nd minute consolation goal through a fierce shot from Deon Burton. But Wise emphasised Chelsea's label as the bookmakers' favourite four minutes later with his second goal after a good one-two with Hughes.
Earlier, Chesterfield also reached the semifinals for the first time in their largely uneventful 131-year history when they beat Wrexham 1-0.

The only goal of a tense, exciting quarter-final against their fellow second division rivals came after 58 minutes and was scored by 31-year-old journeyman striker Chris Beaumont who signed for Chesterfied for a bargain price of 22,500 pounds ($36,000) from Stockport County last summer.
He chased down a long ball from Andy Morris and as Wrexham goalkeeper Andrew Marriott and defender Deryn Brace each left the ball for the other to clear, Beaumont nipped in between them to score.

That was enough for Chesterfield to become the first side from the third tier of English football to reach the semifinals in 13 years and only the seventh in the cup's 125-year history. No club from that level has ever reached the final.
On Saturday, Middlesbrough reached the semifinals for the first time in their history with a 2-0 win at Derby.
The other semifinal slot was being decided later on Sunday with Wimbledon visiting Sheffield Wednesday.
